institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always been very fascinated by French language and society, politics, which is why I've known for a long time that I wanted to do an exchange in France. It could give me access to university courses on French politics.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Academically, it has been very different for the University of Copenhagen, which took some getting used to, but I am left with a lot of new knowledge about schooling and academic culture in France and I would love to go back.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it relatively easy - a lot of information was sent to you by email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I participated in an intro program for a week, if that falls under assistance. Here we were introduced to French methodology and we did social activities around Paris to get to know the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It would have been very difficult if I didn't have French contacts who could put me in touch with their network. I would recommend using your network and double-checking if you don't know your landlord. There are examples of a lot of rental scams in Paris.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Of course, living off-campus is more authentic. However, it was not possible to live on campus in Paris, but there is a university city (Cité Universitaire) that makes up a larger area where each country houses a number of students at a lower rent than the average rent in Paris. I would recommend looking for accommodation there in the first place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sciences Po cannot help with housing as far as I know, so you will have to find your own accommodation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was relatively easy, with several webinars explaining how to do it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The website was a bit rigid. It was first-come, first-served, which made the process a bit stressful and you had to be ready when they opened for registration. In addition, they published an updated course schedule about a week before course registration, which meant I had to apply for courses that I had not been pre-approved for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Webinars, it was also possible to call the Sciences Po administration or write to them by email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to get all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need to be on the clock when course registration opens because popular courses fill up quickly and it's not necessarily clear which ones they are.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was hard and time-consuming with a lot of homework in the form of assignments, presentations, tests and exams, but I really learned a lot that I will take with me.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was similar to the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. I only had one course with a lecture, in addition, I had classroom teaching with up to 30 students approx. called “seminars”. There were presentations from a processor, student presentations and various questions could be asked about the curriculum.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative politics, European integration and it’s challenges: The euro, migration and populism, Europe’s foreign and security policies, FRANCE'S FOREIGN POLICY IN THE MIDDLE EAST FROM 1995 TO THE PRESENT (MIDDLE EAST STUDIES), VIE POLITIQUE, LÉGISLATIVE ET PARLEMENTAIRE FRANÇAISE.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would actually recommend all courses - only the French one if you have a high language level, otherwise it will be too hard I think (B2/C1). All the professors were very ambitious and competent, and they engaged in professional dialog with the students during the semester and gave very useful and detailed feedback.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Transport (Navigo passport) and buying basic food was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was more expensive than I expected. There is only a study discount on the so-called Navigo passport if you are a student in Paris for a whole year.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a wide range of activities such as sports, art, etc. that you could sign up for.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many sports: volleyball, fitness, soccer, yoga, dance. There were also art classes such as painting and drawing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I didn't participate in university programs, but went to several extracurricular activities such as French and dance.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: A lot could be mentioned here, as Paris is a great city to live in. I would definitely visit the city's many museums - it's free for all EU citizens under 25 and many also have student discounts on many cultural experiences.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy, as I had a language level that allowed me to navigate Paris without language barriers.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend going to one or more of the school organized parties or events with guest lecturers. Sciences Po has a large academic network, which provides great opportunities to meet theoreticians/researchers, who do not visit Copenhagen University.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was a bit challenging in the beginning to get used to the late courses. I went to school at 7 to 9 o'clock every monday, which was a bit hard in the beginning.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language, the food culture and the politeness of the French.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You have to be aware that it is a university with a lot of school work, tests and presentations during the semester. If you are prepared and ready for it, Sciences Po will be a fantastic experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is an absence/attendance policy which means that you fail the course if you are absent from more than two classes. I think it is important to draw attention to this.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Certainly, to get a completely unique insight into the French academic culture, which is so different from the Danish one. In addition to meeting students from all over the world, who all share an interest in learning more.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was probably to have to get used to and learn the French method. They have a different way of doing assignments and presentations. It was a bit overwhelming at first, as it was an extra dimension that you have to navigate, on top of reading and preparing for the courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
